title: Building a Nearshore Team That Ships
excerpt: Outcomes first, roles second: how to structure and integrate a nearshore engineering squad.

author.name: Boyo Martínez
author.bio: Boyo leads product and design at NicaSource, where he helps US companies plan, staff and run nearshore engineering teams. He has spent fifteen years shipping digital products with distributed teams across the Americas.

meta.body:
Introduction

Hiring engineers is the easy part. Building a nearshore team that ships, week after week, takes deliberate structure.

Start With the Work, Not the Roles

Before you open a single position, write down the outcomes you need in the next two quarters. The mix of seniority and skills follows from there.

A typical first squad

  • One senior engineer who owns technical decisions.
  • Two mid-level engineers for delivery.
  • A QA engineer embedded from the first sprint, not added later.

Integrate, Don't Isolate

One backlog

Nearshore engineers work from the same backlog, in the same tools, under the same definition of done as your in-house team.

One standard of quality

Code review goes both ways. Senior nearshore engineers review in-house code too, which builds trust faster than any kickoff deck.

The moment a team has its own backlog, it has become a vendor again.

Conclusion

Define outcomes, staff for them, and integrate the team into your rituals from day one. That is the difference between extra headcount and extra capacity.
